assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation framework supplied a highly influential, quantitative account of productivity and cross-country income gaps.
assessment.attribution: The three proposed laureates form a coherent credit group for linking firm-level distortions to aggregate development outcomes.
assessment.maturity: The research program has been extensively developed and remains central to research on productivity and development.
uncertainties: The quantitative size and policy interpretation of measured misallocation remain model- and data-dependent.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collateral constraints and the financial accelerator fundamentally changed macroeconomic analysis of credit cycles.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki, Gertler, and Moore are the central theorists associated with the core mechanisms.
assessment.maturity: The mechanisms have shaped decades of theory, quantitative models, and analysis following financial crises.
uncertainties: The candidate description combines related frameworks whose precise division of credit is difficult to compress into three laureates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection became a foundational lens for measuring trade reallocations and gains from trade.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is indispensable to the canonical framework, while Helpman and Redding made major complementary theoretical contributions.
assessment.maturity: The approach is mature, widely applied, and integrated into modern trade theory and empirical work.
uncertainties: There is a broad set of related contributors, making any three-person allocation incomplete.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Evolutionary analysis of routines and firm dynamism offered a durable alternative to static views of firms and technological change.
assessment.attribution: Winter is uniquely identifiable in the listed candidate, though the intellectual program also reflects foundational collaboration beyond this ballot.
assessment.maturity: Its influence across organizational economics, innovation, and growth is longstanding.
uncertainties: The broad evolutionary tradition makes the boundary of the prize-defining contribution less sharp than for a single formal model.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The listed work gave economics rigorous and influential tools for decision-making when probabilities are ambiguous.
assessment.attribution: Gilboa and Epstein are central to maxmin expected utility, and Marinacci is an important contributor to the broader ambiguity literature.
assessment.maturity: These models have had sustained theoretical influence and applications in macroeconomics, finance, and decision theory.
uncertainties: The empirical scope of ambiguity models and the relative importance of competing formulations remain debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM methods transformed empirical work where persistence, fixed effects, and endogeneity coincide.
assessment.attribution: Arellano and Bond are essential to the original estimator, with Blundell central to its influential extension.
assessment.maturity: The methods are long-established and exceptionally widely used across applied economics.
uncertainties: Their practical reliability can be sensitive to instrument proliferation and specification choices.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian models materially improved analysis of distributional transmission and macroeconomic policy.
assessment.attribution: Kaplan, Moll, and Violante constitute a clear core group for the modern quantitative framework.
assessment.maturity: The framework has already become a major workhorse in policy and academic macroeconomics.
uncertainties: Its comparatively recent development leaves less time to assess its ultimate empirical and policy durability.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work reshaped understanding of how technology and trade shocks alter tasks, local labor markets, and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn, and Hanson are a coherent core for the empirical trade-shock contribution; Katz is also important to the broader research program.
assessment.maturity: The findings have generated a large subsequent literature and substantially informed public debate and research.
uncertainties: Separating the causal consequences of trade, technology, and other concurrent local changes remains empirically challenging.
